newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN RETURN TO TOP WITH WIN OVER COLOGNE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN RETURN TO TOP WITH WIN OVER COLOGNE.

text.p: Early-season leaders Bayer Leverkusen seized the chance to return to the top of the German first division on Saturday with a 4-2 win over fifth-placed Cologne, intensifying a four-way struggle for the title.

Leverkusen had their chance because champions Borussia Dortmund could only manage a 1-1 draw at home to Hamburg on Friday while leaders Bayern Munich were travelling to third-placed VfB Stuttgart on Sunday.

Goals from Markus Happe, Ulf Kirsten, a glorious drive into the top corner from Brazilian Paulo Sergio and an own goal from Karsten Baumann decided the Rhineside derby for the home side, all coming in a pulsating second-half display.
Cologne struck back with two goals in the last eight minutes from Henrik Andersen and Romania's Ion Vladoiu, either side of Baumann's own goal.

"We didn't get going in the first half but I seemed to find the right things to say during the break," said coach Christoph Daum, who established a fearsome reputation for plain speaking when he led Stuttgart to the 1992 title.
The result left Leverkusen on top with 33 points from 16 games followed by Bayern Munich on 32 points from 15, Dortmund on 31 from 16 and Stuttgart on 30 from 15.
The day's shock came at trainerless Fortuna Duesseldorf, who thumped Werder Bremen 4-1 to boost assistant trainer Rudi Wojtowicz's chances of replacing sacked coach Aleksandar Ristic.
Two goals from Russian international Sergei Yuran helped Duesseldorf to their first win in eight matches and lifted them four places into 12th.

The win may also have given another push to the managerial merry-go-round as struggling Borussia Moenchengladbach, winners of five Bundesliga titles in their 1970s glory days, lost 1-0 at home to Duisburg to slip into the relegation zone.

Trainer Bernd Krauss has looked under increasing pressure, and the home defeat renewed speculation that Moenchengladbach, one from bottom, might secure the signature of coach Joerg Berger despite his exploratory talks with Duesseldorf.

The much-travelled Berger has made a name for himself for saving clubs from relegation, but was dismissed by Schalke last month despite taking the club into European competition this season for the first time in 19 years.
Berger's old team have flourished in his absence and on Saturday came from behind twice to win 3-2 at bottom club Freiburg, thanks to goals from Martin Max in the 82nd and 87th minutes.
In the day's other matches, Hansa Rostock beat Arminia Bielefeld 3-1 and 1860 Munich drew 1-1 with Karlsruhe.
